wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: The war with the US has turned into bargaining over the Strait of Hormuz: Putin carried Iran's terms to Trump, and security chief Mohsen Rezaei called Washington's reply to its seven conditions "insufficient". The Guards claimed two mine strikes on supertankers, and Kpler put oil exports through the strait 42% below prewar levels.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: Oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz fell 42% below prewar levels, Kpler says, as attacks on vessels mounted and Iran's Guards claimed mines struck two supertankers. Houthi missiles hit Riyadh's airport twice. Trump's announced energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine pulls the other way, and a Russian lawmaker disputes it.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: Attacks on tankers in Hormuz cut oil exports through the strait 42% below prewar levels, by Kpler's count, and Houthi missiles hit Riyadh on consecutive days. Pulling the other way: a G7 stock release, Saudi Arabia's unexpected price cut to Asia, and Kuwait pumping about 75% of its prewar output.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's gas news was about seaborne supply elsewhere: Pakistan sought 22 winter gas cargoes and may get 12, Iran's gas deliveries fell about 14%, and more Qatari LNG tankers cleared Hormuz. None of it accounts for the US price, which answers to domestic supply and demand.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: Nothing reported this fortnight accounts for the climb; what the news shows is governments struggling to set wheat and bread prices. Pakistan is weeks from sowing with no support price, and a National Assembly committee wants Rs5,000 per 40kg. Egypt postponed a second bread price request from bakeries and mills. India closed its weakest monsoon since 2015.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.
rice.recent: India's monsoon ended 12.6% below its long-term average, the weakest since 2015, and floods in Uttar Pradesh killed 62 as the rains closed. Both came after the last monthly reading, and neither accounts for the path of the price before it.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: China made copper supply guarantees a condition of approving the Anglo Teck merger, and two unions at Chile's Centinela mine decided to strike after talks: buyers are locking in metal while mines keep getting interrupted. India approved ₹1.86 lakh crore for transmission lines, which are strung with it.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: Crude drove this: Brent neared $110 a barrel, and with US inflation above target for 5.5 years most Federal Reserve officials expect another hike by year-end. The selling was global — Japan's 10-year neared a 30-year high and the ECB raised rates in September — while Washington already pays about $1 trillion a year in interest.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley about private credit, the US is paying about $1 trillion a year in interest as bond yields rise, and OpenAI scrapped a model rollout over safety concerns. None of it accounts for the index's gains.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: Washington suspended Microsoft and Adobe from a visa programme over fraud claims, and Microsoft's shares fell 7.5%, a drag from one of the index's largest members. Days earlier, top tech firms signed an accord with Trump to self-police AI development, and Anthropic filed for an IPO. None of it accounts for the wider climb.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The Gulf war and a throttled Hormuz squeezed fuel supply, and September's average of $4.33 was a record, the American Automobile Association said. With the midterms close, a third of states cut fuel taxes, and Trump licensed 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel, which senators from both parties told him to reverse.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Europe buys much of its gas as LNG, and Qatari cargoes have to cross the Strait of Hormuz, where war disrupted shipping and tanker attacks are still increasing. More Qatari tankers cleared the strait at the start of October, extending a rebound. The Bundesbank chief criticised Germany as the risk of gas-driven inflation rose.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: US 30-year Treasury yields hit their highest since 2002 and Bitcoin has had 10 extreme price days this year, but neither the strain in bonds nor the swings in crypto explains what traders were paying for protection on shares.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: President Zardari declared an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under Article 232, shipping containers sealed roads in Peshawar, and Karachi banned gatherings of more than five people. Earlier, Islamabad reviewed a fuel subsidy that 7.6 million riders had registered for. None of it reached the exchange rate.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: Nigeria's story this fortnight was the pump rather than the exchange rate: petrol went from ₦830 to ₦1,400 a litre since February, state-run stations cut ₦66 a litre until 31 October, and Abuja is negotiating a price ceiling. NNPC lost most of its fuel-products revenue. None of it accounts for the naira's rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: Egypt's fortnight was political rather than monetary: Cairo held six Matsda2sh journalists on Brotherhood accusations, and the rights group Emergency Lawyers accused Egypt's air force of a strike that killed 72 gold miners on the Sudan border. None of it accounts for the pound's move.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: Turkey and Pakistan pledged to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia as the Mecca defense pact was activated, and a drone attack sank a cargo ship in the Black Sea off Romania. Neither accounts for the lira's steady weakening.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The news from Bangladesh in these weeks was political rather than monetary: a foreign policy being redrawn away from New Delhi, an envoy's account of Sheikh Hasina's arrival in India, and mob violence testing the country's institutions. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: Indonesia's new finance minister faces a test of delivery, and the rest of the fortnight's news from the country was a prison scandal in Cibinong and a sustainability rating of Chinese mining firms. None of it accounts for the rupiah's move.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The news from Lebanon in these weeks was the war, not the currency: the health ministry put the dead from Israeli attacks at 4,387, a count relayed by TASS, with Israeli troops still operating against Hezbollah in the south. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: The currency itself became a trade dispute: the EU pressed China over its yuan policy as its 2025 deficit with China reached 360.6 billion euros, and Beijing rejected the charges. Macron and Merz sought power to cut off EU market access, and Brussels agreed limits on China's hybrid car exports. None of it accounts for the rate's drift.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: India raised its repo rate to 5.5%, the first rise since 2023, as inflation risks mounted, a move that normally supports a currency. It came while the Sensex was extending a seventh week of declines, and the rupee's weakest day coincided with the US suspending green-card sponsorship for 8 firms, including Infosys.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The real was weakest two days before the first round, when the final debate was cancelled and the US and Australia shut consular services. It firmed after Flávio Bolsonaro beat Lula 47% to 45.1% and forced a runoff; his potential finance chief wants a fast fiscal fix, though Bolsonaro has also pledged pension rises above inflation.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: Nothing in the news from Mexico accounts for the peso's weakening. What it carried was security and weather: 500 US troops deployed to the border over a shooting Mexico says it cannot verify, a deadly prison fight in Sinaloa, and Hurricane Polo's two landfalls on the Pacific coast.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: The ECB raised rates in September and its officials later called the step proportionate, with euro-zone inflation running at nearly double the central bank's target and business activity at a 3½-year high. None of that accounts for the euro's move against the dollar.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Japan's 10-year yield hit 3.11%, near a 30-year high, as a global bond sell-off deepened, and three sources said the Bank of Japan is weighing a declaration that its 2% inflation goal has been reached. Both would normally lift the yen, and neither accounts for its slide.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: Washington licensed Russian diesel sales and Trump said Russia will supply 300,000 tonnes, while EU ministers prepared to blacklist 1,600 Russia targets and 4 Republicans joined 3 Democrats against the deal. The sanctions regimes pulled in opposite directions, and none of it accounts for the rate.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: The fortnight's South African news was domestic: rioters torched cars in Durban and Soweto until an asylum directive was withdrawn, and the state will ask a court to supervise Home Affairs. Gold Fields had an A$39bn bid for Northern Star rejected. None of it accounts for the rand's move.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: Bitcoin has traded against oil this month: a crude rally set off forced selling, with liquidations jumping 235% to $547 million on CoinGlass data, and the price recovered as oil fell despite outflows from ETFs. The US approved its first 3x leveraged crypto funds on 2 October, and MARA has been selling coins to pay for AI.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: The US approved its first 3x leveraged ether funds on 2 October. Days later an oil rally pushed crypto liquidations up 235% to $547 million, and in a $1 billion flush ether bets were wiped out at six times bitcoin's rate. Trump's Iran pledge then underpinned gains across crypto.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: The slide came despite a war, because oil climbed, the US dollar strengthened and bond yields surged, with markets pricing 80% odds of a December Fed hike. Higher rates make a metal that pays no interest costlier to hold. India also ended a tax relief on gold imports, raising costs for its banks.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is the page readers land on when the technology itself, rather than one company or product, becomes the question.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Trump named Jay Clayton AI czar and head of a 'Super Intelligence Force', days after top tech firms signed a White House accord to self-police AI development. That summit came as OpenAI scrapped the rollout of GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns and launched an always-on agent with a $500 paid tier.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: A worker at a plague laboratory in Siberia died and dozens were quarantined; Trump said he would raise the death with Putin. Days later Washington licensed 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel. 4 Republicans and 3 Democrats among US senators objected, and EU ministers moved to blacklist 1,600 Russia targets.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran's Guards say mines struck two supertankers in the strait within days, and Kpler puts oil exports 42% below prewar levels. Tehran agreed safe lanes with Oman but says Washington met only some of its seven conditions for reopening, and a US jet disabled the Panama-flagged Ocean Molica as a blockade runner.

wiki-india.standing: The number of times each day people open the Wikipedia article on India. It is a rough gauge of how much the world's most populous country is on readers' minds, and it jumps when one event breaks through.
wiki-india.recent: Police in New Delhi detained 400-500 people before Saturday's CJP protest at Jantar Mantar, then three former chief ministers, and kept detaining protesters after a Supreme Court ban. Two days earlier the repo rate rose for the first time since 2023. None of it accounts for the earlier peak, which came before all of this.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran holds the strait closed while the US blockades Iranian ports: the Guards claimed mine strikes on two supertankers, and a US jet disabled the Panama-flagged Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman. Kpler puts oil exports 42% below prewar levels. Tehran says Washington met only some of its seven conditions for reopening.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: A ground war has reached the strait's eastern shore. Saudi Arabia planned an offensive against the Houthis, blasts erupted beside a tanker off Mokha, and Yemeni troops say they took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road, with 63 people killed in 24 hours of fighting. None of it explains the summer trough, which came before the offensive.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: The war is at the canal's southern approach. Saudi Arabia planned an offensive against the Houthis, who struck an oil facility near Riyadh, and the Yemeni army says it secured Dhubab, the district beside Bab al-Mandab, where the Red Sea opens to the ocean. None of that accounts for the traffic through Suez itself.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: What surrounded the strait was politics, not shipping: Trump denied asking Xi about potential US arms sales, and the FBI arrested a woman accused of tracking the son of Taiwan's president. Neither interrupted the passage of vessels.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: A 7.7 earthquake toppled a tower in Penonomé on 9 October and set off tsunami warnings across Latin America, but the vessel counts here stop before it struck. Nothing reported in the preceding fortnight accounts for traffic running slightly under its baseline.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Drones began hitting merchant ships across the Black Sea, the water this strait serves. A cargo ship sank off Romania, killing 2 crew, the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan went down off Bulgaria with its crew missing, and a crude tanker burned off Sochi. Ukraine blamed Russia for the first; India protested the last as a Ukrainian strike.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: France spent the fortnight on school protests, a public-sector strike and a dispute with the US over releasing emergency diesel stocks. None of it accounts for the traffic through the strait.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The fortnight's attacks on tankers all fell in the Strait of Hormuz, off Qatar and off Sochi, none of them on the Red Sea route this detour replaces. Nothing in them accounts for the traffic rounding the Cape.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: The fortnight's news from the war was about fuel and sanctions rather than shipping: Ukraine's drone strikes on Russian oil refineries, Washington lifting sanctions on Russian diesel, and the EU preparing its largest sanctions package yet. None of it concerns the strait or accounts for the traffic through it.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Türkiye pledged with Pakistan to send troops to Saudi Arabia under the mutual defence pact the three signed on 7 August, as Houthi missiles hit Riyadh's airport, and Netanyahu ordered an ICC case against Erdogan. None of this accounts for the slide in Istanbul shares.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: Indonesia has a new finance minister, who faces a test of delivery, and the rest of the fortnight's news from the country concerned mining sustainability ratings and a prison scandal. None of it accounts for the fall.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Japan's 10-year yield hit 3.11%, near a 30-year high, in a global bond sell-off, and three sources said the Bank of Japan is weighing a declaration that underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal. Both point to dearer borrowing for Tokyo's listed companies, and neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The trough came in a week when the EU pressed Chinese exporters: Macron and Merz sought power to cut off EU market access, Brussels challenged Beijing over the yuan, and the two sides agreed limits that Brussels says could halve China's hybrid car exports. Beijing then freed 550 billion yuan of unused local borrowing room.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Beijing freed 550 billion yuan of unused local borrowing room, the kind of domestic policy this board answers to, while Brussels pressed China over the yuan and agreed limits meant to halve its hybrid car exports. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: Samsung forecast a record quarterly operating profit of 107.4 trillion won on the AI boom, a 780% jump, and the index fell the same day. The rest of the fortnight was security news: a DMZ mine blast Seoul traced to North Korean forces and a row with Ukraine over North Korean POWs. None of it accounts for the price.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The trough came the day India raised its repo rate to 5.5%, the first rise since 2023, as inflation risks mounted: dearer borrowing lowers what investors pay for future profits. Days later the US suspended green-card sponsorship for 8 firms including Infosys, a weight on the software exporters that anchor the index.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: The banks that carry the index saw a strong rally stutter as bond yields surged. Treasury yields reached an 18-year high, the same climb that sent gold to a 7-week low, and US inflation has run above the Fed's target for 5.5 years.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's Taiwan news was about security rather than business: the FBI arrested a woman accused of tracking the president's son, the first 2 of 66 ordered F-16V fighters landed in Taipei, and Trump denied asking Xi about US arms sales. None of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Annual inflation hit 4.0% in August, up from 3.5%, despite the rate hikes meant to slow it, so the banks that anchor the index got no sign of cheaper money. The miners' exposure is concentrated: China buys three-fifths of Australia's iron ore exports. Firmus scrapped its Sydney listing after seeking a valuation 600 times its revenue.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: South Africa's fortnight was taken up by riots over an asylum directive, withdrawn after 24 cars were torched in Durban and Soweto, and by Navi Pillay's Nobel Peace Prize. None of it accounts for the index's fall: nothing here touches company results, commodities or interest rates.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: Flávio Bolsonaro beat Lula 47% to 45.1% in the first round and leads into the 25 October runoff. His potential finance chief wants a fast fiscal policy fix, which bears on the Brazilian rates this market trades against, though he has also pledged pension rises above inflation.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.
mkt:byma.recent: Argentina gave Britain 2 weeks to halt the Falklands' oil project, and Milei threatened legal action over it, a squeeze islanders describe as economic warfare. None of that accounts for the slide in Buenos Aires shares.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: Canada fast-tracked a 1 million-barrel-a-day Pacific oil pipeline, meant to diversify the economy away from the US, a decision that lands on the energy producers weighing heavily in this index. Nothing else in the fortnight's news accounts for its path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The fortnight's news out of Washington was about rules and deals rather than earnings: crypto's rulebook passed from Congress to 2 agencies, and senators from both parties challenged Trump's diesel deal. None of it accounts for the index's rise.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The ECB raised rates in September and called the step proportionate after euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% from 3.2%, which keeps pressure on it to hike again and raises borrowing costs for German exporters. BMW put €2 billion into German plants while cutting jobs and warning on profit in China.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Schneider Electric lost nearly €15 billion in value on the Monday it bought PTC. Two days later France's central bank chief was saying the country needs no European Central Bank help yet, and Macron and Merz were seeking power to cut off EU market access in a tougher line on Chinese trade.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The one market story out of Amsterdam in the window was about a single stock: BofA said ASML's chip technology move threatens Besi shares. Nothing reported accounts for the index itself.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The weakest days came in a week of political upheaval in Spain: tens of thousands marched after failed housing reforms, police fired rubber bullets at protesters in Valencia, and Sánchez called an early election with his Socialists trailing in polls. Nothing in it touched the banks' own business; what changed was who governs next.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The one piece of news to reach the index's banks was Unipol winning approval from the ECB and the Bank of Italy for de facto control of BPER Banca. That, like the rest of the fortnight's news from Italy, does not account for the fall.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The fortnight's Swiss news was political and diplomatic: the Swiss president was reported to be quitting the government, and India and Switzerland signed 5 pacts on trade, investment and migration. None of it touches the earnings of the companies that carry the index, and nothing here accounts for the price.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: Flydubai suspended its Israel flights after a cockpit attack on a Dubai to Tel Aviv flight that Israeli authorities treated as a terror attack, and Israel ordered 20 British diplomats out of the country. Nothing reported ties either event to the slide in share prices.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Trump said Ukraine should elect a new president and declared an energy ceasefire that Zelenskyy says Russia broke by hitting Kharkiv's power plant. At home, 4 Republicans joined 3 Democrats against his Russian diesel deal, and a judge halted $20 million of Homeland Security ads promoting him.

wiki-united-states.standing: The number of people who open the English Wikipedia article on the United States each day. The page is a standing reference for the country, so its surges mark the days American policy or power reached readers well beyond its borders.
wiki-united-states.recent: Hegseth announced a 3 December firing-squad execution for Nidal Hasan, the Fort Hood shooter, and Trump then sowed doubt on a plan to livestream it. Washington also licensed 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel, which Zelensky called a weak decision and 4 Republicans joined 3 Democrats to oppose.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: Most Federal Reserve officials expect another hike by year-end: inflation has topped the target for 5.5 years and 30-year Treasury yields are at their highest since 2002. But the Labor Department counted 29,000 new jobs against 90,000 expected, so the Fed is seen skipping October. Trump has convened a panel to remove governor Lisa Cook.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: The September hike answered inflation running at nearly double the central bank's target, and officials have since called the step proportionate. Prices then accelerated again, from 3.2% to 3.8% in September, while the euro zone business activity index reached a 3½-year high, so the pressure to hike remains.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: The rise came with a payrolls report showing employers added just 29,000 jobs in September. Days later a NY Fed survey put short-term inflation expectations at a three-year high, so weak hiring and rising price expectations arrived together.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: The fortnight's news belonged to gold, silver's sister metal: it slid to a seven-week low as Treasury yields surged and the dollar and oil rose, then steadied once yields eased. India ended a tax relief on gold imports. None of it was about silver itself.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: The next CPI release is due, and the previews say higher gasoline prices lifted the overall figure, a push that comes from the pump rather than from prices in general. Nothing published in the past fortnight accounts for the climb before that.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: The strait is a war zone with two gatekeepers. The US enforces a naval blockade of Iranian ports and disabled a Panama-flagged tanker in the Gulf of Oman for running it; Iran's Guards claim mine and missile strikes on ships outside the lanes Tehran agreed with Oman. Kpler puts oil exports 42% below prewar levels.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Yemen's government says it retook Mocha, took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road in an advance toward the strait, in fighting that military sources say killed 63 people in 24 hours; the Houthis say they fired 11 missiles at Saudi forces near it. All of that came after the last count of ships here, and none of it accounts for the traffic.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Yemen's government says its forces took Mocha and Dhubab and are advancing on the Bab al-Mandeb, the strait ships must pass to reach the canal from the south, while Houthi missiles struck Riyadh airport. All of that fighting came after the traffic shown here, and none of it accounts for the earlier dip.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: Drought is the constraint: with too little water to work the locks at full pace, ships have been taking the long way around rather than queue for a slot. The 7.7 earthquake that toppled a tower in Penonomé struck after the last reading here, so whatever it did to traffic is not yet in the line.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news concerns this strait directly. The disruption sat upstream in Hormuz, where attacks on tankers cut oil exports to 42% below prewar levels by Kpler's count, and none of it accounts for the traffic here.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.

wiki-israel.standing: Daily views of Wikipedia's article on Israel, a state at the centre of the Middle East's wars and diplomacy. The count jumps when an event sends people looking for background, marking when a story reached beyond the region.
wiki-israel.recent: A Flydubai co-pilot used a crash ax in the cockpit of a Dubai to Tel Aviv flight that landed in Saudi; UAE investigators called it a planned terrorist act, and Flydubai suspended Israel flights. Israel later ordered 20 British diplomats out and shut the British consulate in East Jerusalem. Neither accounts for the earlier peak.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States launches a military invasion of Iran by its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each strike, threat and round of talks.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Traders paid more for an invasion as the talks to end the war stalled: Iran called Washington's answer to its seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz insufficient, a day after Putin carried Tehran's terms to Trump. Iran's Guards claimed a second mine strike on a supertanker, and the Pentagon raised its count of US war dead to 21.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Houthis, the Zaydi Shia armed movement that holds Sanaa and northern Yemen. Its missiles reach the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the southern gate to the Red Sea and Suez.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Houthi missiles hit two Saudi airports, then struck Riyadh airport on successive days, killing 13 and wounding over 300; Lufthansa and Air India stopped flying there. In Yemen the government says it took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road in a push toward Bab al-Mandeb, where fighting killed 63 people in 24 hours.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia, the largest crude exporter and home to Islam's two holiest cities. Its output decisions move the oil price, and its wars and alliances reach across the Gulf and the Red Sea.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: A Houthi missile killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 at Riyadh's airport, which was hit twice. Lufthansa and Air India stopped flying to the capital, and the Houthis declared every Saudi airport a target. Pakistan and Turkey had already agreed, through the Mecca alliance, to deploy troops to the kingdom.

wiki-inflation.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on inflation, the general rise in prices that erodes what money buys. Traffic climbs when price rises and central-bank rate decisions reach households, so it tracks public worry about living costs.
wiki-inflation.recent: India raised its repo rate to 5.5% on a 6-0 vote, its first rise since 2023, and the ECB defended its September hike with euro-zone inflation at 3.8%, nearly double its target. Most Federal Reserve officials expect another hike by year-end. All of it came weeks after the mid-September peak, which nothing here explains.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: A Russian guided bomb killed bus passengers in Kramatorsk a day after a cruise missile hit an apartment block in Pryluky. Then Trump said Ukraine should elect a new president, and Washington threatened to halt the arms Europe pays for under PURL unless Kyiv stops striking Russian oil refineries.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Benjamin Netanyahu will be Israel's prime minister after the next government forms. The price is what traders pay for a yes share, and it moves on coalition arithmetic, polls and his court cases.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: Israel's fortnight was about security, not elections: a Flydubai co-pilot used a crash ax in the cockpit of a Dubai to Tel Aviv flight, Israeli agencies traded blame over his vetting, and a CIA report warned the country risks civil war. None of it accounts for the betting on who leads the next government.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: What traders on Polymarket will pay for a contract that settles at $1 if Kamala Harris becomes the Democratic Party's presidential nominee in 2028. The price is a running bet on her standing against the rest of the party's field.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

stocks:GLXY.standing: A New York crypto financial firm founded by Mike Novogratz that trades, lends and manages digital assets for institutions. It also owns a Texas data-centre campus leased for AI computing, so its share follows both bitcoin and AI demand.

stocks:NVO.standing: The Danish drugmaker behind Ozempic and Wegovy, and one of the world's largest makers of insulin. Its shares trade on demand for obesity and diabetes drugs, and on what insurers and governments will pay for them.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the truce between the United States and Iran survives to a set date. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with every strike, ship seizure and round of talks in the Gulf.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Bettors paid more as the two sides started trading terms: Putin carried Iran's war-ending position to Trump, and Washington answered Tehran's seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iran called that reply insufficient, and the Guards claimed two mine strikes on supertankers in the strait, none of which pulled the price back.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Marco Rubio becomes the Republican Party's nominee for US president in 2028. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a field where the sitting vice-president is also a contender.

poly-will-david-lisnard-win-the-2027-fre.standing: What traders pay for a contract that settles in full if David Lisnard, the mayor of Cannes, wins France's 2027 presidential election. He is a free-market conservative in a crowded field on the French right.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States lifts its blockade of Iran by a set deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with every turn in the talks over the Strait of Hormuz.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Iran said Washington met only some of its seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and security chief Mohsen Rezaei called the US reply insufficient. Putin had carried Tehran's terms to Trump. The Guards claimed mine strikes on two supertankers, and Kpler put oil exports through the strait 42% below prewar levels.

stocks:UAL.standing: The parent of United Airlines, one of the three big US network carriers, with hubs including Chicago, Newark, Houston and San Francisco. Jet fuel is among its largest costs, so its shares move with oil prices and travel demand.

stocks:AXON.standing: The maker of the Taser and of the body cameras worn by most large American police forces, based in Scottsdale, Arizona. Its growth comes from the cloud subscriptions that store and manage the footage those cameras record.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between Israel and Iran is still in force at its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with every strike, threat or stalled talk in the Gulf.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The pressure this fortnight ran through Hormuz and Washington, not between Israel and Iran: Iran's Guards claimed mine strikes on two tankers, Tehran called the US reply to its seven conditions for reopening the strait insufficient, and Putin carried its terms to Trump. None of that explains why the odds moved.

wiki-united-kingdom.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on the United Kingdom each day. It is a rough gauge of when the country draws the world's curiosity, and it jumps on elections, royal events and crises.
wiki-united-kingdom.recent: A suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford, an airbase the US used for the Iran war, brought seven arrests, one of a British-Iranian national, and Iran denied any link. The US then withdrew all 12 B-1 bombers from the base, and Israel ordered 20 British diplomats out of East Jerusalem. None of it dates from the day of the peak.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: Nvidia authorized a record $150 billion share buyback in late September, a commitment to retire its own stock that puts a standing buyer under the price. The same day it launched AI security tools meant to prevent agent breaches, a step beyond chips into software.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Apple Pay launched in India on Axis Bank cards only, without UPI, in a market built around it. Apple also said it will restrict full disk access on the Mac for AI agents, and Rep. Jamie Raskin said the company aided US immigration enforcement. None of it accounts for the share's move.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Google announced Gemini 4 Argon after months of delays and restricted it to trusted cyber defenders over safety concerns; its own benchmarks put Claude 9 points ahead. A judge dismissed the antitrust suits Chegg and Penske brought, and Google signed for 890 megawatts of new nuclear output. None of it accounts for the price.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: Amazon built its 1,000th satellite and is weeks away from starting its space internet service. It also released new Kindles and Alexa tablets that drop the Fire branding before Prime Big Deal Days, then shuffled Alexa's leadership. None of that accounts for the share's move.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: The fortnight's news does not account for the climb, and the largest item ran against it: the Trump administration suspended Microsoft and Adobe from the green card sponsorship scheme over fraud claims, and the shares fell 7.5% after it. A day earlier the company unveiled a new AI Surface laptop.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.
co:broadcom.recent: A survey found licensing costs driving 90 percent of VMware users to explore options, a strain on the software side of the business rather than the chips. Nothing else reported in the fortnight bears on the company, and that alone does not account for the share price.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: Starship reached orbit for the first time in late September, even after losing one of its three main Raptor engines. A nationwide low-band spectrum deal for Starlink Mobile followed, and shares of Verizon and AT&T fell on it. In India, Starlink holds a licence but still cannot sell service.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: Meta launched a paid AI platform for businesses, and its Muse agent topped the US App Store within two weeks, a line of income beyond advertising. In the same stretch a jury in Santa Fe found it deceived consumers 44 million times, and it rushed security fixes after a Muse user could have reached its sensitive internal databases.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: An 11-day pipeline shutdown stopped Red Sea crude loadings at Yanbu, and days after they resumed the Houthis said they had struck an oil facility near Riyadh while two tankers were hit in Hormuz. Saudi Arabia then unexpectedly cut its oil prices to Asia, and Aramco's CEO said replenishing lost supplies could take two years.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla's third-quarter sales fell 2 percent, a result that landed as underwhelming. Its entry into India stalled alongside Starlink's, and Musk's courtship of the country ended in acrimony. Both came in October, so neither accounts for the July fall.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung forecast a quarterly operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, a 780% jump and a figure no technology company has reported before, on demand for the memory that AI systems run on. Samsung and SK Hynix between them control 83% of memory chips, so that spending has few other places to go.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: Micron said memory demand will exceed supply for at least 2 years, and its CEO described supplies as only getting tighter. In a business where prices are set by scarcity, a shortage that long means the company sells every chip it makes at rising prices, with AI demand taking the output.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.
co:amd.recent: AMD agreed on Sep 28 to pay $8.2 billion for World Labs, the world models startup of AI pioneer Fei-Fei Li. That is a chip designer buying a company that builds AI models rather than the hardware they run on.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: Fed officials questioned JPMorgan in early October as part of a review of banks' private credit business, set off by worries about that market. Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley faced the same questions, so the scrutiny fell on the sector's largest lenders rather than on one bank alone.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: Samsung and SK Hynix between them control 83% of memory chips, a concentration that makes Seoul a chokepoint for the AI build-out. Nothing reported in the window accounts for the move in the share itself.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: ASML made a chip technology move that BofA says threatens the shares of Besi. Nothing else reported in the fortnight explains ASML's own price.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.
us-2y.recent: The one story on the subject asked what Washington does next if US bond yields keep rising, not why they rose. Nothing published in the window names a cause for the climb.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.
ez-cpi.recent: The chart stops a month short of the newest figure: September's reading came in at 3.8%, the highest level in three years, and it kept pressure on the ECB to raise rates. Nothing published in the fortnight names what is pushing prices up.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: The fortnight's news was engineering, not price: Solana was scheduled to halve its block times to target 5 blocks a second, the final step of a 200-millisecond upgrade, and the Solana Foundation launched DvP to settle institutional trades in seconds. Neither accounts for the token's move.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: The XRP Ledger added new controls for banks, stablecoins and tokenized funds, and a SPAC tracking the Ripple-linked token jumped nearly 300%. XRP bids piled up in Q3 while Ether's liquidity shrank against bitcoin. None of it accounts for the price.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.
doge.recent: Dogecoin got an Ethereum-style testnet for trading, lending and stablecoins at the start of October, the kind of plumbing the coin has never had. In the same days Bitcoin's lift from a soft inflation reading faded as bond yields refused to fall. Neither accounts for the price here.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: Developers released Udon into the network's shared cryptography library and began moving Tachyon code into faster private-payment software. Gemini switched its Zcash software ahead of 25-second blocks, which then went live on a public testnet ahead of schedule. The drop from the peak came as Bitcoin slipped too.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.
link.recent: The peak came a day after Chainlink launched CCIP 2.0, an upgrade that gives big crypto apps more control over their own security when they use the network. Nothing else reported in the window explains the earlier trough or the retreat that followed.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: For a decade the Bank of Japan held rates near zero on the argument that underlying inflation was still short of its 2% target. Three sources told Reuters the bank is weighing saying this month that the target is roughly met, which removes its own stated reason to hold. Oil prices since the war on Iran have raised Japanese import costs.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The fortnight's argument was about China's currency, not its rate. The EU pressed Beijing over a ballooning trade deficit and charges of yuan manipulation, and the PBOC backed its FX policy as the yuan hit a four-year high against its basket. None of it touched the policy rate.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia's own news this fortnight was about its balance sheet, not its policy: international reserves fell 4.85% in September to $731.76 bln, and it made no yuan purchases or sales in early October. None of that accounts for the rate.

wiki-petroleum.standing: The crude oil pumped from underground and refined into petrol, diesel, jet fuel and the feedstock for plastics. It is the world's most traded commodity, and its price runs through transport, food and inflation everywhere.
wiki-petroleum.recent: A war has throttled the Strait of Hormuz: Kpler counted oil exports through it 42% below prewar levels, and Iraq began trucking crude through Syria to bypass it. Aramco put the supply lost at almost 3 billion barrels and said replenishing stocks would take two years.

stocks:DAL.standing: One of the three largest US airlines, flying from hubs including Atlanta, Detroit and Minneapolis. Its share price moves on jet fuel costs and on demand for business and premium travel, and it reports results before its rivals.
stocks:DAL.recent: Delta cut its profit outlook after saying fuel will cost it $6 billion more this year, even with demand for seats holding strong. That is a squeeze on margins rather than on sales, and it arrived at the very end of the window, so it does not account for the share's earlier climb.

stocks:LLY.standing: An Indianapolis drugmaker whose tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro for diabetes and Zepbound for obesity, made it the world's most valuable pharmaceutical company. Its share moves on demand, pricing and supply of that one drug class.

stocks:LHA.DE.standing: Germany's largest airline group, owner of Swiss, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines and Eurowings. Its profits turn on jet fuel costs, long-haul business travel and wage deals with pilots and cabin crew, whose strikes ground it.
stocks:LHA.DE.recent: Lufthansa stopped flying to Riyadh, as did Air India, after a Houthi attack on the airport there killed 3 people in Saudi Arabia. One suspended route is a small piece of the network, and it came at the end of a slide that was already weeks old; nothing else reported in the period accounts for the share.

stocks:MARA.standing: One of the largest listed bitcoin miners, running power-hungry data centres that earn new coins and keeping a large reserve of them. Its share tends to move with the bitcoin price, amplified by what its power costs.
stocks:MARA.recent: MARA has been selling the bitcoin it used to accumulate: holdings fell by 18,245 coins between February and August to pay down debt and build AI computing infrastructure. This week about 996 BTC, worth $81.1 million, moved to an address a chain-analytics firm identified as Galaxy Digital's.

stocks:KEL.KA.standing: The private utility that generates, transmits and distributes electricity to Karachi, Pakistan's largest city, listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange. Its plants burn imported gas, and a state regulator sets what it may charge.
stocks:KEL.KA.recent: The utility is short of re-gasified liquefied natural gas: cargoes are late because of disruption to global supply, and it warned it may cut power at evening and night peaks as an extreme, last-resort measure. No cuts have been ordered. The warning came after the share's slide and does not by itself account for it.

stocks:CSCO.standing: A San Jose maker of the routers, switches and security software that carry corporate and internet traffic. Its orders are read as a gauge of how much businesses and telecom carriers are spending on networks.
stocks:CSCO.recent: 10 countries signed trade deals with Washington that limit which telecom suppliers they may buy from. Terms like these decide who is allowed to sell network equipment in those markets, which is the business this company is in.

stocks:LMT.standing: The world's largest defence contractor by revenue and the maker of the F-35 fighter. Most of its sales come from the US government, so its share moves on Pentagon budgets and on foreign arms orders.
stocks:LMT.recent: The first 2 of 66 F-16V fighters Taiwan ordered landed in Taipei, and the US Navy plans to put the stealthy AGM-158C anti-ship missile on B-52 bombers. India's air force chief said the US had made no official offer to sell it F-35 jets. None of this accounts for the fall in the share.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: Thai inflation accelerated again, with floods adding to the price risk, as a widening Middle East war drove dear oil and diesel into import bills. Finance ministers gathered in Bangkok for the IMF and World Bank meetings under that energy shock and rising interest rates. None of it pins the index's slide on a single event.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Houthi missiles hit Riyadh's airport repeatedly this month, one strike killing 13 and wounding over 300, and the group declared every Saudi airport a target. Lufthansa and Air India stopped flying to the capital, and Pakistan and Turkey agreed to deploy troops to the kingdom, putting a war inside the city where these shares trade.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: Two shocks landed on Dubai's doorstep. A flydubai co-pilot used a crash ax in the cockpit of a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, which Emirati prosecutors call a planned terrorist act, and the airline suspended its Israel flights. Then shipping through Hormuz thinned to seven ships in a day, the fewest since 23 July.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-us-pr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Marco Rubio wins the 2028 US presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with his standing in the Republican field.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: Meta turned its Muse agent into a product line: a paid AI platform for businesses, an expansion to small businesses, and an app that topped the US App Store within two weeks. A Santa Fe jury found it deceived consumers 44 million times, China unwound its buyout of Manus, and a Muse flaw that left internal databases reachable was fixed in a rush.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, YouTube, Android and the Waymo robotaxi business. Most of its money comes from search advertising, so its share is a reading on the ad market and on whether AI erodes or extends search.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Chegg and Penske lost their antitrust suits against Google over its AI, and the company signed for 890 megawatts of new nuclear output. Its new Gemini 4 Argon went only to trusted cyber defenders, and Google's own benchmarks put Claude 9 points ahead of it. All of it came after the share had already risen.

stocks:INFY.standing: India's second-largest IT services exporter, based in Bengaluru, selling software and outsourcing work to Western companies. Most of its revenue comes from North America, so US visa rules and tech budgets reach its share.
stocks:INFY.recent: The US suspended green-card sponsorship for 8 firms, including Infosys, which said it sees no material impact. The PERM programme governs whether a skilled foreign worker can stay permanently, not whether they can be billed to a client, so the firm's revenue is untouched while its engineers' path to residency stops.

stocks:WIT.standing: One of India's largest IT services firms, based in Bengaluru, selling outsourced software work and consulting to companies abroad. Most of its revenue comes from US and European clients, so their tech budgets and visa rules reach it.

stocks:TCS.NS.standing: India's largest IT services company, part of the Tata Group, running outsourced software and consulting for banks and corporations, mostly in North America and Europe. Its results gauge global corporate tech spending.
stocks:TCS.NS.recent: The shares rose on quarterly results: revenue grew 11% to ₹73,188 crore, driven by AI work and international business. TCS also built a higher bench and increased subcontracting as it prepares for demand, hiring ahead of contracts rather than after them.

stocks:CTSH.standing: An IT services and outsourcing firm based in New Jersey with most of its staff in India. It runs software for US banks, insurers and health companies, so its share moves on corporate tech budgets and US work-visa rules.

stocks:MSFT.standing: The world's largest software company, maker of Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, and OpenAI's biggest backer. Its share is among the heaviest weights in US indices, so index funds worldwide move with it.
stocks:MSFT.recent: The US suspended Microsoft and Adobe from its green card sponsorship scheme amid fraud claims, a ruling on whom the company may hire from abroad. The same week it unveiled a new AI Surface laptop, and Satya Nadella called for a human able to halt any model mid-task. None of this accounts for the share price.

stocks:XPEV.standing: A Guangzhou-based maker of electric cars, listed in New York and Hong Kong. It designs its own driver-assistance software and chips, and sells into the most crowded and heavily discounted car market in the world.
stocks:XPEV.recent: XPENG branded its robotaxi business YOYO and on 8 October opened sign-ups in China by invitation code, a step beyond tests limited to its own employees but not a commercial launch. The car runs on four of the company's own Turing AI chips. The share's slide came before that announcement, and nothing reported accounts for it.

wiki-yemen.standing: The number of people who open Wikipedia's article on Yemen each day. The country sits on the Bab al-Mandab strait at the mouth of the Red Sea, so a war there reaches the shipping that runs between Europe and Asia.
wiki-yemen.recent: Houthi missiles hit Riyadh's airport on consecutive days, killing at least 3, and Lufthansa and Air India stopped flying there. On the ground, the Saudi-backed government says it took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road beside Bab al-Mandab, in fighting that killed 63 people in 24 hours, military sources say.

stocks:CMCSA.standing: The largest home broadband provider in the United States, and the owner of NBCUniversal, with the NBC network, Universal's film studio and theme parks, and Sky in Europe. Its earnings turn on households keeping a cable line.

stocks:DIS.standing: The share price of the entertainment group behind the Disney, Pixar and Marvel studios, the theme parks, Disney+, ABC and ESPN. The parks earn most of its profit, so it trades on household travel spending as much as on streaming.
stocks:DIS.recent: Disney went back to layoffs at the end of September, a fresh round of job cuts on top of earlier ones that deepened anxiety among its workforce and was described as leaving "a much smaller organization". The share's trough came the day after that news.

stocks:PSKY.standing: The owner of the CBS network, the Paramount film studio and the Paramount+ streaming service, controlled by the Ellison family. Its earnings turn on whether streaming grows faster than cable television shrinks.

stocks:FOXA.standing: The owner of Fox News, the Fox broadcast network, Fox Sports and the streaming service Tubi, controlled by the Murdoch family. Its income is cable fees and advertising sold against live news and sports.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.
